utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope that -- I'm hearing other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. Okay. Good morning, everybody. I hope we can now move on. We are at the stage where the -- the Defence is still cross-examining the witness, but before we start I was made to understand by the legal team that there might be a request that we sit this afternoon one session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Our request would be that if the cross-examination is not completed by the end of the regular morning session, that we would perhaps continue into the afternoon, in the hopes of finishing this witness today. He does have other duties with this team and, to some extent, with other teams. And while he's been able to come to the Tribunal during his testimony and do some limited work, he's very much limited in the -- the inability to communicate with us of course, and to some extent with other teams, and we thought that might be a possibility to wrap up his testimony today, Your Honour. That was the only suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you are probably best-suited to give us an indication as to whether we are likely to wrap up the cross-examination of this witness or the examination of the witness this morning. Are you able to make any contribution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the plan of the Defence is to finish our cross-examination today, although the duration of the cross will depend on the expert witness's answers, whether they will be short or more extensive. I do hope that we will be able to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, the -- the other problem that I've sort of -- that has been reported to the Chamber is that we're falling behind with scheduling of witness, and there's a new witness who is scheduled for next week Monday. And the idea is to try and wrap up this witness today. In any case, I hope we can do that, Mr. Milovancevic. My attention has also been drawn to Rule 90(H), which does require that the Chamber makes sure that we wrap up the examination of witnesses as expeditiously as possible. Okay. I wouldn't want to waste more time. Can we then move on to the witness -- or, I see Mr. Black has something to say. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Something very brief. We filed a Rule 89(F) motion earlier in the week, I believe on Tuesday, with regard to a witness who will come to testify viva voce at the beginning not of next week but the following week. We failed to request expedited consideration in the written motion, but we have since realised in order for us to prepare that witness for the following week we'll need a decision, which could be oral, by sometime next week. So I was going to ask if the Defence could, if possible, file any response by Monday or Tuesday, we'll then file any reply immediately, I would say the next day, with the hopes that Your Honours would have time to decide the motion by the end of the week, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, is the Defence in a position to file an answer to the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will do that within the time limit on Monday or, at the latest, on Tuesday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milovancevic, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we left it off on page 84, the SAO Krajina TO, Territorial Defence. In paragraph 2 entitled evolution from January to April, and then on the following page, paragraph 3, evolution between April 1991 and December 1991, you describe the development of the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina. Is it right that between April and December 1991, the staffs and units of the TO were established in different parts of Krajina that you mentioned in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, but I would like to add that when we talk about staffs, it's the staffs on the local levels. A staff on the SAO Krajina level was, according to the documents I reviewed, only established at the end of September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 86 of your expert report, under paragraph 5, Adoption of the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia, you stated that on the 1st of August, 1991, the government of the SAO Krajina adopted a decision to apply the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of this SAO Krajina. Do you know that the Croatian parliament on the 21st of February, 1991, took a decision to sever all its constitutional and legal links with Yugoslavia and that all the areas that had been governed by federal laws would from that time on be governed by that republic alone?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I've mentioned before, my report is aimed at studying and analysing the SAO Krajina TO as well as the RSK TO and the SVK, and relation between these armed organisations and Milan Martic, and I've also indicated earlier during my cross-examination that therefore I didn't study legal decisions and other issues related to Croatian armed forces in detail for the purposes of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the law on defence of the Republic of Serbia, which it had been decided to be applied in the territory of the SAO Krajina, whether in fact it was in conformity or in compliance with the constitution of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's a legal question which would require legal analysis and, as I've mentioned earlier during my cross-examination, I'm not qualified for these matters and therefore I wouldn't want to express any opinions which may be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in the parts of your expert report where you deal with the legislative provisions regulating defence, especially in section 2 where you analysed the legislation of Serbia, that's to say pages 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, did you quote all the relevant legislation from the Republic of Serbia dating from 1991 which had to do with defence affairs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I -- as Mr. Milovancevic pointed out correctly, I listed these articles, but I didn't analyse them. I just listed them in order to be able to better understand the decision that was taken at the SAO Krajina level on the 1st August of 1991 to adopt the law of defence of the Republic for -- of Serbia as the law of defence of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in all the pages that I enumerated, Mr. Theunens, you compared the provisions of the -- those laws with the provisions of the SFRY legislation with the 1982 All People's Defence law. And based on that you drew your conclusions that the TO, the Republic of Serbia, constituted the armed forces of the SFRY and conclusions to that effect?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I did is - and that is explained on pages 61 and page 62 of the English version of my report - I quoted article 5 of the 1991 law of defence of the Republic of Serbia as well as the article 6. And the article 6 in its paragraph number 1, which is mentioned at the top of page 62 of my report, states, I quote, so we're talking about the duties: "The president of the republic in organisation of defence preparations commands the armed forces in peacetime and in war, thus including the authorisation for realisation of organisational and personal issues in territorial defence." Now, what I did then, I compared it to the articles 113 and 115 of the 1992 All People's Defence law --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Theunens. I did not wish you to analyse again all the articles you cited and which you described in great detail. My question to you was whether you compared the provisions of the federal legislation and the Serbian legislation, and did you come across any provisions which, to you as a military expert, would point to the fact that the given provision was not in accordance with the SFRY constitution. That was my question, and please do not go into detail in analysing matters that we've dealt with here before.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, to answer the question, what I did was I compared paragraph 1 of article 6 of the 1991 defence of the Republic of Serbia with articles 113 and 115 with the 1982 All People's Defence law, and I wrote down based on that comparison there was a lack of coherence, and this is on page 62, because the 1982 All People's Defence Law mentions that the arm -- that the TO is subordinated to the SFRY Presidency, whereas article 6 of the Serbian law of defence states, as I mentioned, that it's the president of the republic, i.e., the Republic of Serbia who commands the armed forces. That's all that I did, and I did -- because of the fact that I'm not a legal expert, I didn't think it would be appropriate to go into further details on this matter. I merely pointed out what looked -- what seemed to be a contradiction or at least a lack of coherence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The law of -- on defence of the Republic of Serbia, in your opinion, does it contain a provision to the effect that the TO of Serbia is part of the unified armed force of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the question in the sense what is meant with the concept of "unified armed force of Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I misspoke. I meant the unified armed force of SFRY.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, the -- as mentioned on page 57 and page 58 of my report, the article 31 of the 1991 Serbian law on defence states that: "Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia is a part of the united armed forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. On page 89, do you state there that the Krajina Assembly took a decision on the 29th of May, 1991, electing Martic to the post of minister of defence of the SAO Krajina. That's page 89 of your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, and this decision is included in 65 ter number 79.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you state in paragraph 1 on page 90 that on the 27th of June, 1991, Milan Martic was re-elected minister of the interior of the SAO Krajina, re-elected?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I put the "re" in re-elected between brackets because even though I didn't make an analysis of the role, on one hand, of the secretary, and, on the other hand, a minister of internal affairs, I understood that it was merely a continuation of the occupations Milan Martic occupied before, and even though -- that is included in the chart I prepared for Your Honours, that on the 29th of May, 1991, a Mr. Dusan Vjestica was appointed minister of interior, and I don't -- I didn't include -- that's -- sorry, that can be found back in 65 ter number 80, which is not included in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you please keep your answers short. If your answer is affirmative, as it was in this case, then please answer with a "yes."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 89, at the top of the page, did you not state that on the 29th of May, 1991, the SAO Krajina Assembly promulgated the constitutional law?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the constitutional law of the SAO Krajina, it also adopted a law on ministries.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that can be found on page 89 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since you state in paragraph 1, page 90 that since January -- 4th of January, 1991, Martic had been secretary of the internal affairs, you start your sentence by saying that: "On the 27th of June, he was elected minister." Does it mean merely that the new law came into application and that under the new law he was now styled as a minister of the interior and not the secretary, as before. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I answered the question before, but then the answer was considered too long. Between 4th of January and 29th of May, 1991, Martic was the secretary of interior. 29th of May, 1991, he was appointed minister of defence, and on the same day, Dusan Vjestica was appointed minister of the interior. However, on the 29th of June, 1991, Milan Martic is, if I could use the expression, is re-appointed or is elected minister of the interior; and that's my answer to that question which I already gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The -- do you state on page 91 that on the 8th of August, 1991, Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic minister of the interior. Did he not appoint him minister of defence? Therefore, Milan Martic, who was both minister of the interior and minister of defence, had been appointed deputy commander of the Krajina TO. That's page 91.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe it's an issue with the translation, but page 91, paragraph 7, states that: "Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic, who was the minister of interior and minister of defence of the SAO Krajina to the position of deputy commander of the TO of the SAO Krajina. It didn't -- the paragraph does not say that Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic to the position of minister of interior, nor does it indicate or does it say that Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic to the position of minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarity. Are we looking at paragraph 7 on page 91?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And doesn't it say clearly that on that date, the 8th of August, 1991, Milan Babic appointed Milan Martic minister of interior and minister of defence of the SAO Krajina to the position of deputy -- well, what does it say? Does it say: At that stage Martic was both minister of interior and defence but then was now also appointed to the position of the deputy commander of the TO or does it say he was appointed to all those three positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to indicate the first option you mentioned, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So he was already at that time minister of interior and minister of defence, and he was being appointed minister -- deputy commander. Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That's as much as we have to say about the power struggle between Milan Babic and Milan Martic. Now let's move on to page 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in paragraph 9 you say on the 30th of November, 1991, the SAO Krajina adopted its own law on defence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you quote article 31 of the law on page 94 which says that the: "SAO Krajina TO is considered to be part of the unified armed force of the SFRY"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed that's article 31 of the SAO Krajina law of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 99 of your report under (f) 6cap?, that's last paragraph, you state that: "The commander of the 2nd Lika Brigade of the SAO Krajina, Petar Grbovic" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Petar Trbovic, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: -- "requested Milan Martic to remove a group of soldiers led by Predrag Baklajic who had been training at the camp in Golubic and that this order demonstrated Martic's position vis-a-vis the subordinate TO commanders"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The reason I mentioned it is because by that date, on the 12th of November, 1991, we have already a staff for the SAO Krajina TO and also a commander for the SAO Krajina TO. And I'm not sure, but I think it's still Colonel Ilijas Djulic at that stage. And we discussed earlier the appointment of Milan Martic to the position of deputy commander of the territorial defence on the 8th of August. The decision we have does not indicate which would be the duties of Martic. Normally in the military context, a deputy commander is most of the times or in most cases responsible for logistical aspects and for the running of the staff. For example, the Chief of Staff actually will be the deputy commander in a traditional military environment, and he plays the commander when the commander is not available. Now, again, Martic, 8th of August, deputy commander of the TO, we don't know for how long he occupies that post, but what we know is that by the 30th of September there is a commander for the TO and there is no information on who the deputy commander is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That was not the gist of my question, Mr. Theunens. My question focussed on the fact that colonel -- that Petar Trbovic wrote a letter to Milan Martic, wherein he told him that the mentioned Predrag Baklajic had promised to cooperate with the Territorial Defence but that he refused to do so, that he abandoned the first line, and that later on he came back and called on the men to desert their positions. At the same time, many people from the surrounding places speak of a group which does not engage in combat but rather in looting, and they call them renegades. Can you tell us what sort of order are you referring to here? Was this an order issued by Martic to Trbovic or vice versa? What do you base your conclusion as to this superiority -- or rather, this superior/subordinate relationship between Martic and Trbovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you answer. Isn't it quite clear from this paragraph, Mr. Milovancevic, that obviously if - I don't know how to pronounce this - but Petar Trbovic makes a request to Martic to remove somebody, it means Martic has the power to remove that somebody, in the view of Trbovic. And that's the basis for the conclusion. Isn't that as simple as all that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all respect, Your Honour, this is a wrong conclusion because Mr. Theunens mentions a group trained at Golubic, and by doing so ties Mr. Martic in with the group. At the same time, he has a letter which shows that this is a renegade group, does not engage in combat, but rather in looting, and he is asking for assistance in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Milovancevic, if the conclusion is wrong, tell him the conclusion is wrong. Don't ask him to confirm what is already written in the paper. He has written it in the paper. He makes his conclusion based on the fact that somebody is appealing to this man, who is supposed to be a superior, to do something about a situation that he doesn't like. And that's the basis of the conclusion. And if that basis is wrong, just tell him: "Your basis is wrong."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what is the basis of your conclusion that Mr. Martic is superior to Baklajic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think the easiest would be if we all see the document. It is 65 ter number 1256, but in any event what I tried to explain in the conclusion is actually what Your Honours mentioned, it is that Trbovic believes that Martic is a person with authority and with the authority to remove this group of Predrag Baklajic. When you look at the document it starts with: Comrade Martic, and then there's a long description, and it ends with "friendly greetings." At least in military language --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where can we find that document? Can we get it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's exhibit 1256 from the 65 ter exhibit list. 1256, therefore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we have the 65 ter exhibit list with us? I don't think I do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document is on the monitor, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have it still.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So from the heading we can see it's an order of a document with a top secret number 1/10. Commander of the Lika brigade to the SAO Krajina, it doesn't say which ministry, but it -- "to the attention of Milan Martic," and then it says "Comrade Martic." When we scroll down in the document we see at the end, the last paragraph: "We ask you to remove the aforementioned and his group." And then he says: "Friendly greetings, Commander Colonel Trbovic." As I said, "friendly greetings" I have not seen that mentioned often in all JNA officers to other people. My impression -- or my analysis -- basically, my analysis of this document is that Trbovic believes that Martic is a person with authority and that Martic is the one who is in a position to remove Predrag Baklajic's group. If Trbovic had followed, let's say, military procedures, he would have sent a letter to the commander of the Territorial Defence. There was a commander at that time. And that commander would then -- if Baklajic's group was subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior, well then the command of the TO would have contacted his counterpart on the level of the Ministry of the Interior or the police. But it -- I mean, the explanation given by Mr. Milovancevic does not make sense from the military point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Before you proceed, counsel. So would you agree then that the document lends an interpretation that Martic was a person of influence but not necessarily superior to the person who addressed the letter? Is there any room for that interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. Now, with regard to superior, at least de jure, there's no indication of a subordinate/superior relationship. De facto, then of course we enter into the area of influence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What is the basis of your conclusion that there is actual influence? Do you not in paragraph 3 mention this captain of special forces and are you aware of the fact that Baklajic was in fact arrested for serious crimes and was ultimately murdered?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mentioned earlier, all I can say on the basis of this document is that Trbovic believes that -- or considers that Martic is a person with influence who is able to fulfil this request of removing Predrag Baklajic's group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 103 in paragraph (c) did you write that: "On the 10th of October, 1991, Milan Babic, as president of the SAO Krajina, sent a report to the chief of the General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, confirming that the TO of the SAO Krajina had been established in accordance with the order of the chief of the General Staff of the SFRY"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, and this can be found in exhibit 65 ter number 167.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 105 of your report in English, do you state in the very first paragraph that: "During the operations in the mentioned areas in Croatia towards the end of the winter in 1991, an order was issued to achieve and maintain single command over the JNA and local Serb TO units." And then you also mention the order of General Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, the only difference is that the paragraph says "orders were given," not just a single order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. In the last paragraph on that same page, 105, do you state that: "The JNA established operational and tactical groups in order to create conditions for or to restore, maintain, single command and control over all forces involved in combat." And do you then list forces which took part in combat operations, namely, JNA, local Serb Territorial Defence forces, local Serb police, and Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and the details follow on the following pages. I would just like to add that in Northern Dalmatia I didn't come across any documents as far as Northern Dalmatia is concerned. I didn't come across any documents as far as the local Serb and local Serb MUP to the JNA was organised through operational and tactical groups; it was mainly in the other areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I put these two questions to you, Mr. Theunens, because on page 105 you quoted directly the order of General Vukovic dated 26th October, 1991, where in item 1 it is stated that: "The resubordination pertained to the TO units in the territory in the area of responsibility of the 9th Corps." No other order has the title that you seem to use "local Serb TO," "local Serb police," "Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia." Where else did you see these terms used? You are the only one who seems to use them. Do you actually change the terminology used by the JNA units in the field?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was not my intention to change any terminology, but I believe that for the reader it would be easier to understand that when "TO" is mentioned, for example, in this order quoted by Mr. Milovancevic, we are not talking about the TO of the Republic of Croatia as it existed actually prior to the conflict, but of a TO which was mainly manned and established by, call them, Krajina Serbs or local Serbs because there were also local Serb TO units in Eastern Slavonia and Baranja. And that was my only intention. I -- my -- it was my impression that the use of "TO units" as such would be misleading or even confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since you're an expert, isn't it much more precise to say "Territorial Defence units in the area of responsibility of the 9th Corps" or any other unit? Isn't that a proper, precise terminology? And can you mention any unit of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia by its name and military designation which participated in any combat operations in the Republic of Croatia? And this is what we're discussing here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we would have used Territorial Defence units in the area of responsibility of the 9th Corps, there would still have been a risk of confusion about whether these were mainly Serb organ -- I will rephrase this. Whether these were TO units which were actually established by Krajina Serbs, or whether it were TO units of the Republic of Croatia. I think it's clear from the -- from my report and from -- in particular from the documents I have used to compile my report that these TO units were not units of the Republic of Croatia, but were self-styled or self-established units which were controlled and commanded by the JNA and which were manned by people from areas known as the SAO Krajina. As for the second part of the question, unfortunately it's not included in this report, but I can easily identify that during the break, if that can be of assistance of the Court. When we look at the area of Baranja and Eastern Slavonia, so in the Eastern part of Croatia, there is an order from the 1st Military District or a report from the 1st Military District at the end of September 1991 where they list at least 21 units or detachments of the TO of the Republic of Serbia that are involved in operations in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem. Again, this specific order is not included in this report because I only talk about SAO Krajina TO. And at that part -- at that time, the local Serb TO in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem was not yet part of the TO of the SAO Krajina or the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that those were the JNA orders of an authorised command of the JNA. In a situation when the constitution stipulates that the armed forces are constituted of the JNA units and the TO units which can be considered forces for manoeuvres. Isn't that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, Your Honours, but I only mentioned this an attempt to answer your question when you state, Mr. Milovancevic, that there are no -- that no units with the Republic -- with the TO of the Republic of Serbia were involved in the conflict in Croatia. I didn't go into further details in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 106, under (ii) you mentioned 18th of August, 1991, and an order by Milan Martic, whereby he warned the police department in Split and Kijevo as well as local commune in Kijevo that he would not tolerate the presence of Croatian police in his territory, giving them a 48-hour deadline to withdraw. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and in the order is even -- Martic is more specific. He calls these police stations "upholders and guardians of the Ustasha and fascist policy of the so-called non-Croatian democracy."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Mr. Martic, as a policeman, wrote a letter to the Presidency of the SFRY to the Federal Secretariat of the Interior in Belgrade and to the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia on the 3rd of March, 1991, warning them that barricades had been erected in Kijevo, that the locals had been armed, and that, as much, they threatened the delegation of the Municipal Assembly of Knin, and that they sent back the Knin SUP members from that area? This is exhibit 244 on the 65 ter list. Have you seen such a document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't specifically looked at that document, Your Honours, because it referred more to purely police matters, whereas my report deals with military issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In that report dated 3rd of March, 1991, Mr. Martic gave a public announcement saying that the population of the local commune of Kijevo is used as a victim intended to provoke Croatian police for these purposes that I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see exhibit 244 on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, has this been already admitted into evidence, this exhibit you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm aware, not, Your Honour. This exhibit has not been mentioned at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English version is 02170655.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you please read out --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph of this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, shouldn't the document be tendered into evidence before we start reading it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was about to move for that to be done after we have gone over the contents. But, yes, I will agree with your suggestion, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But how do you go through the contents before it's part of the evidence? If it's admitted -- if it's not admitted, how do you deal with the fact that you've dealt with it already? If this is the witness you want to tender this document through? Does this witness know anything about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this has to do with an operation conducted in the village of Kijevo. This document pertains to the village of Kijevo and to the operation which was concluded in August of 1991. This document is on the exhibit list of the Prosecution. The Defence believes this document to be an important one because it shows the motives and reasons for an event. This is why we believe this document to be important. The witness uses this operation in Kijevo to say something about Milan Martic as head of police in Knin. This is a document sent by Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do understand what you say, Mr. Milovancevic, but I would imagine that the Rules of Procedure in -- should be followed. And I thought there is a specific procedure for tendering exhibits into evidence. Anyway, you say that it's -- it comes from the list of documents -- list of exhibits -- it comes from the exhibit list of the Prosecution. I don't know -- we'll hear if there's anything from the Prosecution on that. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, would you please tell us: To whom is this document addressed, the one dated 3rd of March, 1991? Would you please read out the addressee's name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The addressees are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you said you were tendering it before you -- you start reading it, Mr. Milovancevic. I thought you seemed to accept my suggestion that it must first be admitted into evidence before you start reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move to have the OTP exhibit 244 admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the document will -- is admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit. May it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 105, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Who is this letter addressed to, Mr. Theunens? Would you please read out the heading.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is addressed to the Presidency of the SFRY, Belgrade; the federal SUP, Belgrade; and then something, I don't know what it means, OF MUP Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just at that point, Mr. Milovancevic, I'm sorry to do this to you. Would it be convenient to take the break here? I'm mindful of the fact we started 15 minutes late, but so that we don't confuse our schedule for the day, I'd like us to keep to the time. Would that be okay if we took the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the court will adjourn and we'll come back at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that delay, but we had to sort out the issue that we were talking about this morning of sitting this afternoon. From the point of view of the Bench, if it is convenient with everybody else, it would be preferable, if we do sit, to sit at half past 2.00 for one hour and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That would be fine with the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Obviously this means that the lunch break would be much shorter than usual. And how is it with you, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And is it okay with everybody else, the interpreters, the other staff?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would need to consult all booths again and come back to you later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please can you do that. I would appreciate that very much. Thank you so much. Mr. Milovancevic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We left off at the point where we were discussing the Kijevo police station and Martic's warning issued on the 18th of August, 1991. The accused, Martic -- in that letter containing warning that Mr. Martic sent on the 18th of August, 1991, does Martic advise and warn the population of Kijevo to find safe shelters in order to protect themselves in case of a military operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, even though the safe shelters, as such, is not specified. So it's not clear whether it's meant -- it means that the people have to leave Kijevo or whether they can go to areas within Kijevo where they are protected or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The norms of international laws of war, do they provide for precisely this type of a duty, that should there be any military operations in a certain area where civilians reside, then these civilians need to be warned of the upcoming military action?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honours, of international -- of the laws of war is that attacks on civilian targets or civilian facilities should be avoided.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you are evading the answer. I'm not asking you about what your understanding; I'm asking you about the provisions of the international laws of war and whether there is a duty on the part of warring sides to warn the civilian population. Let us not waste time any longer, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may be correct. But, again, I answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, that's sufficient, Mr. Theunens. On page 107, paragraph (iii), do you state there that the international mediator -- or rather, the chairman of the international conference on the former Yugoslavia sent a complaint to the SFRY leadership due to the destruction of churches and religious buildings in Kijevo during the JNA operations, whereas Mladic wrote a report justifying what had happened?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the footnote you marked that report by Mladic as Exhibit 1237, so could we please see this on our monitor. This comes from the OTP 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I imagine this would be already into evidence as part of this report? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can quickly check. I'm not sure off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, it is a footnote here -- it is on the footnote, so it must be part of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I misunderstood Your Honour. It's certainly part of the report. I don't know off the top of my head if it's one of the ones I put into evidence during direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this exhibit was not tendered into evidence; it was mentioned in the expert report and based on my recollection it was not entered into evidence. Therefore, I move for it to be exhibited as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear your application, Mr. Milovancevic, but I was thinking that because this report -- or what we have admitted is just what has been mentioned during -- yeah, you are right. It will then be admitted into evidence and may be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 106. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have this now on your monitor, this letter -- or rather, the report by General Mladic on the 4th of October, 1991, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, we still have the letter by Milan Martic that was briefly mentioned before the break on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's helpful, I note that while the B/C/S version of this document comes up okay, the English is not finding it. So we're going to check on our side to make sure it got into e-court all right, and I'll report as soon as I know something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. It doesn't look like we have the English --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, while we're waiting for the English version, could I put some questions to the witness pertaining to this document, and then later on we can check the document itself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned this document in item 1, do you remember that General Mladic in item 1 says that: During the combat for Kijevo on the 26th of August, 1991, the units waged a multi-hour battle in order to lift the siege in the area of the village of Civljani and that the greatest resistance was provided by the units of the National Guards Corps from the Catholic church which contained a machine-gun nest and the headquarters of that unit. In the course of that combat, the commander was captured. Do you remember such a report by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I remember the report and I also remember that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I also remember that this is the version General Mladic gave of the events at Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in this report General Mladic states that: From the area of the church and from the cemetery which is near the church, there were very well-fortified shelters built by concrete -- built with concrete blocks. So from the area where the church is located and from the cemetery, other forces of the National Guards Corps opened fire, and these units were composed of reservists hailing from Postar [phoen] near Split, that after five years [as interpreted] of fighting for Kijevo, when further progress was impossible towards the besieged unit, they opened fire, first from an anti-aircraft machine-gun, calibre 12.7 millimetre. And when that failed to chase the ZNG members from the church, they opened fire from a cannon. The church was not destroyed, rather the bell-tower was hit as well as one of the walls. Do you remember this explanation provided by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, indeed I mentioned -- I remember that this is what General Mladic writes in his report about the events in Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that General Mladic wrote that TV Belgrade had made a report about the church in Kijevo, the monastery, and the Kijevo graveyard as well as the Vrlika monastery which was used to house a hospital for the ZNG as well as war materiel depot?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is what General Mladic writes in his report about the events in Kijevo, but if we really want to focus in detail on what happened in Kijevo, I didn't analyse the events as such; and if I were to analyse the events, I would have also looked for other sources that described the events in Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Counsel for the Defence, before you proceed, on your first question there's a reference to five years of fighting. Is that actually correct? It's in section 25 or 26 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, five hours. It should read "five hours." I may have misspoken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: That should be corrected for the purpose of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does the international law of war provide for religious buildings to be deprived of their privileged status once a state of war has been declared?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not aware of that provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question has been interpreted as if the privileged status would be lifted for such places of worship, whereas my question was: Is it not the case that during war operations these places of worship do continue to enjoy their protected status? However, once they are used for military purposes, the protection is lifted and these facilities are no longer protected facilities. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. Put as such, I am familiar with that provision of international laws and customs of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us the reason why you left this detailed explanation by General Mladic out of your report. You, by doing so, not only insinuate that the accused committed the crime, but you turn this comment by Lord Carrington into an accusation. Why do you that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, on page 107 where -- in this Roman -- this subparagraph (iii), I spoke about -- I mentioned that Carrington complained to the SFRY about the destruction of churches and religious buildings in Kijevo, I just mentioned that to indicate, well, indeed that the operation that took place there, and I also included the fact that Mladic wrote a report on report how he had handled the situation in Kijevo. And I actually I write "Mladic wrote the report to justify how the situation was handled." We only have the account by Mladic. It was read out now. Now, whether what Mladic writes is correct or not or is an objective comment or not, I am not in a position to comment on that. The main reason I included the section on Kijevo is to show that it's -- or to mention it as an example where forces of the SAO Krajina police operated together with the JNA and were subordinated to the JNA during those operations. I don't think I insinuate anything in that paragraph and I don't specifically talk about crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you concealed from the Trial Chamber and the Defence the fact which you omitted to mention, which was that there were combat operations going on in Kijevo, that the other side had machine-gun emplacements, that the battle went on for hours. You presented the event in an entirely different light and, in essence, you accused Martic of the entire event.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may well be the opinion of Mr. Milovancevic, but I would like to draw your attention to the fact that I did include a reference to the report by Mladic. It's the footnote 304, and it corresponds with the exhibit 1237. If I really had had the intention to hide anything or to do what you suggested I am -- that I did, why would I have put the footnote number then in the document? Why would we have had the opportunity to discuss the report by Mladic then?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If you're asking me to answer this, Mr. Theunens, then this is my question to you: By omitting this, isn't it quite evident what your intention was? But let's move on. On page one hundred and --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: -- 17 you mentioned Skabrnja-Nadin.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I mean, something is suggested, I gave an answer. The footnote number is there, the reference number is there. If the Chamber wants to consult this document, all the reference material is there, so I don't really see a problem. The situation in Kijevo is included in a section not on crimes but a section on subordination. So if I considered that Kijevo was a crime, then I would have analysed in it detail, consulted more sources than just the report of Mladic, and I would have included it on the section on crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's move on to page 117 to the issue of Skabrnja-Nadin, Northern Dalmatia, where you mentioned the Croatian side complaining --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting Your Honour. Just before we move away from that document, I said I would report back to the Trial Chamber. We're trying to work it out so that the English appears in e-court. There's some sort of technical difficulty, but we'll deal with it hopefully at the break or as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Black. Are you happy with that arrangement, Mr. Milovancevic? Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on page 117 of your report you mention Skabrnja and Nadin, and the complaint by the Croatian side addressed to the European Community Monitoring Mission about 30 people who had been slaughtered in Skabrnja. In this context on the next page you mention reports by Major Branislav Ristic and Simo Rosic, including the report by Ernest Radjen a lieutenant. Is that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, and in the footnotes you can find the exact footnotes for these documents, if you wish to consult them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the material you studied, did you come across the information that in the village of Skabrnja a Croatian irregular unit was positioned, an armed irregular unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the report by Lieutenant Ernest Radjen, which is the 65 ter number 1271, makes a reference to -- I'm not sure the presence of a Croatian -- what you call irregular unit or the presence of what was called -- or I called Ustasha symbols is included in Radjen's report, exhibit 1271.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your work, did you come by information that in Skabrnja in the surrounding villages, the commander of the Croatian forces there had over one -- over 700 armed men in his command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may be possible, but I didn't come across such information. In any event, I think that what I've included in my report, i.e., I included the report by JNA security officers, Ristic and Rosic, for the purpose of describing or trying to describe that took allegedly place in Skabrnja Nadin. I believe that the information included in the reports of Ristic and Rosic is very helpful in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to this information, did you study the notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic, that's OTP exhibit 1489.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it please be shown on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Until the document is shown, can you tell us whether you are familiar with the notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic? That's Exhibit 1489.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I've seen these reports before, but I don't recall exactly what is included in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In these notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic, which were kept on the 18th and 19th of November, 1991, they were handwritten, and the OTP had translation made of relevant part, and these pages bear the number 0206872 and 020087075.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see these pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Here Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic had said on the 17th of November in Skabrnja two JNA officers were killed five were wounded. One armoured vehicle of the JNA was destroyed, and that seven armed Croatian soldiers were captured, 15 of them were killed, and five 82-millimetre mortars were captured from the Croatian side, one 60-millimetre mortar as well, one 120-millimetre mortar. Do you recall that, Mr. Theunens? Can you see that on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that exactly, Your Honours, and I don't see it on the monitor. But it may well be correct, but again what we're talking about, the reports of two JNA security officers, Major Ristic and Lieutenant Commander Rosic wrote about crimes in Skabrnja --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise for interrupting you. We'll get to both the gentlemen Rosic and Ristic. Can you just briefly tell us whether you recall that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please see the relevant part of the document on the monitor. The relevant portion of the text is at the bottom of the page. The note dated 18 November 1991. Can it -- can it be scrolled down a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have before you the text of the notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic which has to do with the situation in Skabrnja on the 18th of November, 1991? Do you have that before you, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I can see the top of the page where, according to the notes, General Vukovic - I assume this is the General Vukovic who was the commander of the 9th JNA Corps - gives instructions in order to have preparations made and mop-up the villages of Skabrnja and Nadin in the course of the 18th of November, 1991. Yeah, and here --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it now on the screen? Could you please read the last paragraph at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 15: "18th of November. Razovljeva Glava - railway station - Crkva Svetog Luke, St. Lukas church, stretch taken over. Circular defence has been organised. Skabrnja and Nadin have been partly encircled. MPs are in control of mopped-up parts. In combat activities around the village of Skabrnja there were: Two killed, two wounded plus two from TO," and then it says the rest of the line illegible. "Seven captured Ustashas. 15 killed Ustashas. Seized: Five 82-millimetre mortars, one 60-millimetre mortars."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. On the next page, the next day of notes by Bogunovic is the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please be shown the combat report for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The report is located at the very bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "19th of November, 1991. "The operation of cleansing Zemunik, Skabrnja, and Nadin from Ustashas was finalised at 1700 hours. "Gradina was taken over. "In combat activities there were: Two killed, two plus two plus one wounded, one tank and one armoured tank damaged, no Ustashas killed, except for one foreigner (Kurd), eight Ustashas captured. Seized: Five 82-millimetre mortars, one 60-millimetre mortar, one 120-millimetre mortar."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. In the two days of combat in Skabrnja, the JNA seized a total of 14 mortars; however, on the 19th of November -- or rather, the OTP did not have the entire entry of the 19th of November translated because in handwriting it also says that 50 automatic rifles were -- was -- were seized, one recoilless gun, 35 hand-grenades, seven crates of 7.62 ammunitions, and one hand-held rocket launcher. On the basis of these notes by Lieutenant Colonel Bogunovic, can it be said that what happened in Skabrnja was an armed conflict between the JNA forces and the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, Your Honours, that the notes of Colonel Bogunovic, the ones I see now, speak about what seem to be combat operations between the JNA. And in the notes of the Bogunovic, the other side are called "Ustashas."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 118 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I -- I move that this exhibit 1489 be tendered as a Defence exhibit, and can we please be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 107, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 118 of your report, you mention the report by Lieutenant Ernest Radjen dated 1 December 1991, and you state that the report mentioned the killing of civilians that occurred during the operation in the village of Skabrnja. Is that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the quotation marks refer to the section where it says: "Defeating Ustasha forces in the village of Skabrnja." I would have to see the document to be able to answer the question of Mr. Milovancevic. Because it could be that what I mention about "killing of civilians" is based on what I read in the reports drafted by Majors Ristic and -- Major Ristic and Lieutenant Commander Rosic, who used the word "killings."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the OTP exhibit 1271 be shown on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned it, Mr. Theunens, in the -- in -- in the footnote 338 in relation to Radjen's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please take a look at the exhibit. While we are waiting for the document to be shown on the screen, we can proceed with the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Theunens, that Lieutenant Ernest Radjen wrote the report as a member of the military police of the military post 4810 in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Theunens, that Lieutenant Radjen in the introduction of his report wrote the following: "In crushing the Ustasha forces and securing the front line and mopping-up, I came by the following information," and then he enumerates the information. Do you recall this part? It will be shown on the screen in a moment.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall it, Your Honours. It would be helpful if we could scroll a little bit down. Okay. Yeah, that's fine. Indeed, and now I also see that in the first paragraph Radjen writes about -- okay, the fighting in Skabrnja on the 18th and 19th. And he says: "... about 50 people of various ages, members of paramilitary Ustasha formations and civilians at various locations in the village ... were killed," and then he explains how the people in the villages were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Theunens, what the "sanitisation of an area" means. Is this something that is not only governed by the international laws of war, but even mandatory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, sanitisation or cleaning -- clearing-up of the battle-field can mean many things. In the purely military sense it can mean -- it means that resistance pockets -- enemy resistance pockets are still remaining, have to be removed. It can also mean that, actually for hygienic reasons dead corpses or even dead bodies have to be removed. Now I would like to draw your attention also to the 65 ter number 2060 which is explained or which is mentioned on page 112 of my report. It's at the bottom. It's an order, number 01-47-3, where a Captain Divljakinje [phoen] of the SAO Krajina Glina TO talks about mopping-up of the terrain, which is actually the same as sanitisation. And he speaks about the "requirement to make a distinction between Serbs and non-Serbs" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that was not my question. My question was what sanitisation of a battle-field means. In other words, does it imply the obligation of a warring party to remove the bodies of men, carcasses, and to undertake other such activities to avoid infection and to ensure the sanitary conditions of the territory that it has under its control? Is this not even something that is governed by international laws of war and are you familiar with it or not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the counsel also said: It is not the mopping-up of the area. It doesn't mean to mop-up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, of course Mr. Milovancevic is correct. But I've seen it also used -- like here, the word "clearing-up" is used as the English translation. Now, basically we would have to compare the B/C/S documents with the original wording in order to be able to say whether Radjen means cleaning-up, mopping-up, or sanitising the battle-field. But I am familiar with the term "sanitising" the battle-field. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In this report in items 1 through 21, the report by Lieutenant Ernest Radjen, is it clear that he toured all locations in the village, and that wherever he found a casualty, he wrote down that casualty's location, injuries, clothes worn by that person, whether the person was armed or unarmed, whether the person was in the house or outside the house? And that in addition to the list of all victims - and there were a number of victims -- or rather, more victims than reported - he also attached a sketch of Skabrnja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please see the top -- the first paragraph of the top of the document. Yeah, I mean, from this document when we look at it as the only source we cannot establish when Radjen tours the battle-field. The document is dated the 1st of December. The events took place on the 18th and the 19th. If you go down a bit, please. Do we know whether Radjen was on the spot when the people were killed and is therefore in a position to exactly determine how, when, and why the people were killed? Therefore, I also include the reports by -- I mention Ristic and Rosic, because they also provide information on the circumstances of the killings in Skabrnja and Nadin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are there reports different from this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the other reports, the reports by Majors Ristic and Commander Rosic talk more about the issue -- about the investigation of a crime that took place. And they mention alleged perpetrators and the organisation of the groups that allegedly perpetrated the crimes. This report here focuses on the nature of the victims and the condition in which they were found. So I think it would be advisable to look at all available documents and not just the one by Radjen in order to be -- to determine what happened in Skabrnja and Nadin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in order to remove any misunderstandings, I'm not claiming anything firmly; I'm just putting questions to you. My question is as follows: On the 1st of December Mr. Radjen wrote his report. And on the 20th of November, a day after the combat in Skabrnja, Croatia lodged a protest with the European mission, the mission of the European community. In your view, does this show that the victims didn't lay about for ten days in yards and in the streets and so on without being cleared away and buried? What Lieutenant Ernest Radjen wrote, doesn't it indicate that he went to the spot immediately after the event and noted down all the details? That was all I asked you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at least I cannot conclude from the document when Radjen went there. I assume that indeed he went there prior to the 1st of December, but my answer to the previous question was that from the document we cannot determine whether Radjen was there at the time of the killings or whether he came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The report by Major Ristic, Commander Simo Rosic, do they speak of the suffering of the civilians -- or rather, the killing of the civilians and do they indicate who the possible perpetrators might be? Obviously during the combat, civilians got killed. Some civilians got killed, and these people are now reporting about this. Do they mention perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, Ristic and Rosic mention alleged perpetrators in their reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, did -- were these people ever prosecuted by the Office of the Prosecutor of The Hague Tribunal? It's been 15 years since the event.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's a question that should be asked to me. I mean, I'm not aware of any particular prosecution of the perpetrators in Skabrnja. Now, I'm familiar with the mandate of the ICTY, and I think that mandate is sufficiently clear to explain why these people are not perpetrated and why other people have been indicted for the alleged crimes in Skabrnja and Nadin. And I meant to say that these people are not investigated or indicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. The next village in Croatia that you mention is Saborsko. Do you know whether in Saborsko there was any armed conflict or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The situation in Saborsko, the military operations there, discussed between page 108 and 111; and from the JNA orders I reviewed, it can be concluded that there was an armed conflict in the area of Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the order of Cedomir Bulat commander of the 2nd Tactical Group which you mentioned precisely in the pages that you just told us, were orders issues in that document to lift the siege of the barracks in Licka Jesenica attaching also a list of persons who were located in Saborsko, namely 400 people armed with two Brownings, which are anti-aircraft machine-guns, and an anti-aircraft gun, also armed with 20 machine-guns and a number of automatic and semi-automatic rifles? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I quote from several orders by Cedomir Bulat. It could be that it's indeed mentioned in one of the orders that determined the tasks of Tactical 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you come across an OTP document entitled: "The war log of Tactical Group 2" or "2nd Tactical Group"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I came across, but I didn't include in my report. Because this section here deals with the issue subordination, and it was -- the documents I looked at, JNA orders for the Tactical Group 2, as well as Operational Group 3 and from the 5th Military District were sufficient, in my view, to establish the subordination relationship that existed between the JNA and the local Serb order SAO Krajina TO in that area during the time period that is relevant for this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In this war log of the 2nd Tactical Group, did you see that continuous assaults of Croatian forces, from Saborsko, from Glibadol, from the Alan elevation, and from the surrounding area were carried out daily on the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th November of 1991 before the operation for clearing-up Saborsko began?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may well be possible. I -- as I mentioned, I didn't include that war diary in my report. The documents I included -- for example, I see one here, 1257, which refers to an attack on Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we be shown exhibit 1248 on the monitors, which is an operative diary of the 2nd Tactical Group, commanded by Colonel Cedomir Bulat, who was also in command of the Saborsko operation. I also tender this OTP exhibit into evidence as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 108, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. While we are at the point of exhibits, Mr. Milovancevic, exhibit number 107, that is the last exhibit before this one, I'm made to understand has got, it's about 200 pages in B/C/S, and I think only 19 pages have been translated. Now, the question to you is: What actually do you want admitted into evidence of these 200 pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution translated only 19 pages which are relevant for the Skabrnja event. I propose that these 19 pages be tendered. Out of that material we covered only two pages pertaining to the 18th and the 19th, and that's are the two pages that are relevant to us, only those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. Then let the record show that Exhibit 107 is made up of 19 pages, the translated pages into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Furthermore, Your Honours, the report by Ernest Radjen, 1271, should also be tendered into evidence. We just covered it with Mr. Theunens. The report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The report by who?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reports 1271, report by Ernest Radjen, lieutenant, on the 1st of December, 1991, about the sanitisation of the area in Skabrnja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. But that report will then be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 109. Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You have before you, Mr. Theunens, the English translation of the handwritten document which is operational diary of the 2nd Tactical Group. Can you confirm to us that under items 2 through 9 there is mention of daily combat and assaults, serious assaults, against the barracks in Jesenica and Slunj.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page, please. I can see the items 2 to 4 there is fire -- the fire exchanges. In items 5 it says: "They suffer under heavy fire from Saborsko and Glibadol on barracks. They gave the coordinates." I assume "they" refers to a JNA unit, but it's not really clear from the document. Item 6 speaks about: "Very heavy attacks on the barracks by ZNG." Item 7 -- at least there's one entry for JNA opening fires -- ordered to fire from artillery weapons. It also shows item 7, actually, there's cooperation between JNA and TO Plaski, which at that time is SAO Krajina TO. Article 8 -- excuse me, entry 8 mentions that the barracks are defended. And then item 9, okay, the body of a dead soldier is evacuated. I think there's one entry that specifically mentions attacks on the barracks, and then, maybe if I recall, two entries that refer to serious combat activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, under item 2, is the barracks in Slunj mentioned on the 4th of November, 1991? Is it stated that: "Around 2200 hours, the forces of MUP and ZNG opened small arms fire on the barracks, wounding soldier Spasimir Vasilec?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it says that the ZNG and MUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Just a brief answer, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but -- I mean, if you ask me a question -- it doesn't say under which circumstances under which soldier Spasimir Vasilec was wounded. It can be assumed from this entry that it's because of the fighting, but again we don't know who wounded him. He was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Under item 3, the date is 5th November, 1991. Does it read there that: From the area of Glibodolski Kriz, that in that area there was an activity of ZNG and MUP forces towards the Licka Jesenica warehouse and that this continued until 2200 hours?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Item 4, date 7 November. Does it state there that the forces of Plaski TO were fired upon from Browning and mortars. They were fired upon by ZNG forces and the attack was launched from Saborsko, Bozin Vrh, and other directions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, firing and attacking are not necessarily the same activity. You can also -- when you're like in entrenched positions, you can open fire without attacking your opponent, and that's firing. Now, if -- when you're carrying out an attack, attack implies also movement. So I don't see that the word "attack" is being used in this entry. It just says that TO forces from Plaski are being fired upon from ZNG forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. Theunens. That's awhile what is written there. Item 5, does it say on the 7th of November heavy fire was opened from Saborsko and Glibadol against the barracks, and then they gave coordinates. Most likely this pertained to artillery.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, Your Honours. It mentions heavy fire, heavy fire is normally associated with artillery, but it's weird that in the other entries the type of weapon is identified, 4, 6, but here it just says "heavy fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The first attack we mentioned on the 7th of November, was it 2.50 a.m., meaning during the night?
