And then under item 6 on the 7th of November it says: "1630 hours," and then it says: "Very heavy attack on barracks in Licka Jesenica by ZNG. They fire from artillery weapons, calibre 130-millimetres, on the region Mala Kapela, Glibodolski Kriz, the basin of Vrletna Draga [phoen]," and so on. Is that right, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mentions indeed a very heavy attack by ZNG, that is correct. But then the next line: The fire opened from the artillery weapons, 130-millimetre on the region, I think we would need to have a map to determine who was whether, and in order to include whether it's the ZNG that opens fire with the artillery or whether it's somewhere else. For me, from just these two lines, it's difficult to draw that conclusion. If Mala Kapela and Glibodolski Kriz are under the control of the JNA and the SAO Krajina TO, then it's reasonable to assume that the artillery fire, the 130-millimetre, comes from the ZNG, but I cannot draw that conclusion from only this entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you conclude that based on item 8, which says: 7th of November, 1991, at 2000 hours. "One soldier was killed, the barracks defended." And then the body of that soldier was, on the following day, evacuated by helicopter out of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, but the entries do not mention the circumstances under which the soldier was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In item 17 and 18, does it say that on the 12th of November the operation against Saborsko began as planned, that two planes bombed an industrial zone in the area of Slunj? And does it say in item 18 that on the 12th of November at 1600 hours the operation was completed and Saborsko liberated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the war diary says, Your Honours, for the entry -- for number 17 and number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what Slunj is and -- facilities in Slunj, what kind of JNA facilities existed in Slunj? Slunj is in the vicinity of Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that -- and actually Mr. Milovancevic mentioned it. There is what we call a polygon. It was a major training area. I'm not sure for which kind of units this training area could be used, if it was an infantry training area or also for artillery and tanks. I also know that at one moment in time the headquarters of the 5th Military District from Zagreb had to be evacuated, the 5th Military District of the JNA, evacuated to Slunj. I also know from the 1991 census that I think there was something like 63 per cent of the population in the Slunj municipality was of Croatian ethnicity, and then a bit more than 30 per cent of the population was of Serbian ethnicity. Slunj is located on the major road that goes from Karlovac to Asta [phoen] south, so to Titovo Korenica. And if you want to achieve territorial integrity [Realtime transcript read in error "majority"], particularly in the case of the SAO Krajina, control over Slunj and the villages around it, including Saborsko, was essential. I didn't say "majority," but I meant to say "territorial integrity."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in Slunj there was a reserve command post of the 5th Military District, the main command post was in Zagreb, and a reserve command post of a strategic JNA formation with all fortifications and other equipment was located in Slunj?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned what I know, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the training grounds in Slunj were built in an area populated predominantly by the Serbs, who had to be moved out because the training grounds were built there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is possible, but that was not the subject of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. On page 120 you write that the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 743 on the 21st of February, 1992, establishing -- or rather, deploying the UN peace mission to Yugoslavia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could phrase it like that, Your Honours. 743 allowed the deployment of UNPROFOR, whereas earlier resolutions only allowed the deployment of what were called United Nations liaison officers who were to prepare the UNPROFOR mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 122 you say that in January of 1992, the constitution of Krajina defined the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina as armed forces of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Is that true, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. It's article 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how is it that such a provision on defining the armed forces could constitute a violation of the Vance plan, when the Vance plan was adopted almost two months later. This provision was adopted in January, and the Vance plan was adopted on the 21st of February.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am not familiar with the Vance plan -- the fact of the suggestion that the Vance plan was adopted on the 21st of February. I think -- I mean, we discussed it already earlier. On the 23rd of November, a cease-fire agreement is signed in Geneva. On the 3rd of January, an interim agreement -- an interim agreement and cease-fire is agreed upon by the commanders of both the Croatian forces, as well as JNA. But at that time the negotiations for the implementation of the Vance plan were already ongoing. So 743 is just one part of the implementation of the Vance plan. When I use -- when I say in my report the declaration of the SAO Krajina TO, that it would be the SAO Krajina armed forces could be considered a violation of the Vance plan, I meant by that that it could be considered a violation of the spirit of the Vance plan. Because as I mentioned on -- when Mr. Black asked me that question, I said: Well, as long as you don't implement this article, it's fine. If you start implementing this article about the armed forces, it represents a violation of the Vance plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One short question before the break, by your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Vance plan provided, on the basis of what Goulding agreed upon with the warring parties, that until such time as UNPROFOR forces reached the area, Croatian legislation should not be applied in the territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we notice that there was an error in the interpretation. My question was: Does the expert know that the Vance plan explicitly provided for the areas where the UN forces are deployed until -- for the duration of their deployment there and until the resolution of the crisis, those areas should not apply -- or the Croatian legislation should not apply in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this or not, Mr. Theunens? Just a brief answer.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this -- this comment you make, but I'm not sure whether it's included in the Vance plan or whether it was raised during the meetings Marrack Goulding had with representatives of Serbia and SFRY in February and March 1992. In any event, the UNPAs [Realtime transcript read in error "UNPO"] were determined or declared -- or the UNPAs were areas within Croatia. So that's the key issue, I think in the whole discussion. It should be "UNPA," United Nations protected area. They were determined as areas in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we take a break at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would be the appropriate time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do so, let me just mention that the Chamber has received the communication that the interpreters are able and amenable to sitting at half past 2.00 this afternoon for one hour, 15 minutes. We shall, therefore, reconvene at half past -- I beg your pardon. At that -- during that session, we'll sit from half past 2.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We were discussing page 130 -- or rather, let's move to that page where you discuss the transformation of the RSK TO into RSK special police brigades. In paragraph 2, do you not say that on the 28th of April, 1992, the SSNO ordered that eight police brigades be set-up on the territory of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And the term used in the document, which is 65 ter 1334, is "Milicija Brigades."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 133, do you not refer to the order on demobilisation issued by General Milan Torbica on the 23rd of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And I assume that Mr. Milovancevic speaks about Exhibit 65 ter 2072.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Theunens. That's the document. In this order, did General Torbica state under item 1: "With the demobilisation and withdrawal from the for -- should be finished on the 24th of August [as interpreted] in the entire territory of the RSK and the territory should be taken over by special police forces"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's a translation issues, Your Honour, but General Torbica says that the front line is being taken over by the PJM forces, so the special police forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask, in terms of the time on the deadline you mention 24 of August, but here I read 24th of June and then completion by 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. I must have misspoken, if that was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does not item 2 state: "The withdrawal of the troops, artillery tanks, and PVO equipment is to be carried out as per the plan compiled earlier in cooperation with the special police units and the UNPROFOR forces"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does item 4 state: "From the 1st of August until the 15th of August, 1992, store all weaponry and other technical equipment, seal the repositories, regulate their security with the special police units, and solve the issue of the documents of the killed or the wounded through the municipal organs"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does item 5 state as follows. "According to the rate at which the weaponry is laid down and by the 15th of August, 1992, at the latest, switch to regular work hours and to wearing the civilian clothes in all the HQs, commands, and TO RSK institutions"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is indeed what the paragraph 5 says, Your Honours. Now I would like to add that the Vance plan stipulated that the areas were to be demilitarised and that then the UNPAs were to be demilitarised and that the TO, local Serb TO, was to be disbanded and demobilised. Disbanding means that military structures are dissolved. Now, if people continue to work in commands, headquarters, and RSK -- TO RSK institutions, that indicates that the military structures are actually not dissolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We will get back to that issue a bit later, Mr. Theunens. Under item 7 of this order by General Torbica, does it say that the TO members are forbidden to carry -- from carrying firearms in public, except the firearms for which the bearer has a regularly issued license, as for all the other citizens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that's what paragraph 7 states.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does item 11 read that: "Duty rosters for the zone staffs, brigade commands, municipal TO staffs, and the 75th Infantry Brigade Main Staff of TO are to be organised and to wear civilian clothing"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, but I -- again, I would like to refer to the earlier comment I made on the stipulation of the Vance plan and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My question to you was only what the order read. We know what the Vance plan read. I apologise for interrupting you, but I've received your answer.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I finish the answer or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. So I would just want to add in relation to paragraph 11, that I wanted to refer also to what I said earlier about dissolving of the military structures, i.e., the dissolution of the local Serb TO, the SAO Krajina TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Vance plan precisely provides for the terms disarming, demobilisation, and disbandment, and that it discusses provisional disbandment of staffs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, the Vance plan provides for disarming, demobilisation, disbandment. The disbandment does not only apply to staffs, but it applies to the entire local Serb TO. And again, if you want to have the exact wording, the best would be to look at exhibit with 65 ter number 917.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does the Vance plan envisage for the TO staff to receive their salaries from the local authorities? Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with that. I'm not sure whether it mentions TO staffs, but I'm familiar with the fact that the Vance plan prescribes that former TO members are to be paid by the local authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We mentioned the UN Secretary-General's report on the resolution on UNPROFOR. This is S24600, the resolution S24600. I don't think this's any need for the document to be shown on the screen right now. Is it correct that in this particular report, let's say paragraph 4, where it says that: "The first stage of demilitarisation was implemented successfully, that the JNA had fully withdrawn, except for one element of the forces near Dubrovnik, that the TO was demobilised, and that the weaponry was stored in warehouses under double lock." This same report referred to the problem of special police units. Is this a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the reference S24600 is not sufficient for me to determine which report of the Secretary-General we are talking about. It would be helpful to have a date for the report or to have the report shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The date is 28th September, 1992, report S24600, exhibit number 1360. You quoted it. My question to you was as follows. Paragraph 34 of the report says that special police units constitute that the main problem in the UNPA zones, starting from July 1992 through to the period of the submission of the report. Do you remember that part?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, but I would prefer to have the report shown because it would be easier to see the entire paragraph 34 and also 35. I know that the report talks about the problems raised by the existence of these special police units, but if you want to discuss specific issues it would be helpful to have the report in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this report be shown, please. Can paragraph 4 of the report be shown, that's the next page -- or can you please scroll up in order for us to see paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you read for us where the paragraph 4 says that the first part of the demilitarisation process was implemented. Can you read that portion, please?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's the first sentence. "The first two phases of demilitarisation proceeded well. The Yugoslav People's Army (General) completed its withdrawal from Croatia, with the single but significant exception of the Dubrovnik area, and the Territorial Defence forces demobilised, placing their weapons in storage depots under a double-lock system. However, the complete demilitarisation of the United Nations Protected Areas has been delayed by a violation of the United Nations plan, which was referred to in my report of 27 July. This is the creation of new Serb militia forces designated variously as "special police," "border police," or "multi-purpose police brigades," made up of former members of the JNA, the Territorial Defence forces, and irregular elements, which may total as many as 16.000 armed men, equipped with armed personnel carriers, mortars, and machine-guns. The authorities of the so-called Republic of Serbia Krajina" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's enough, Mr. Theunens, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we read paragraph 4 fully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. " The authorities of the so-called Republic of Serbian Krajina hereinafter referred to as the Knin authorities, claim these are police units. The force commander considers that their level of armament and their almost total ignorance of police work show that, in reality, they are paramilitary forces. UNPROFOR has vigorously protested this violation of the" -- then we would need to scroll down to the next page. "... of the United Nations peace plan and has pressed repeatedly for the demobilisation of these newly created units and for the regular police to be armed only with sidearms in accordance with the plan."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see paragraph 7 on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you read for us what the Serb side presents as the explanation for the existence of these special police units.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The justification given by the Knin authorities for these forces is that they are needed to defend Serb-controlled areas from attacks and infiltration by the Croatian army. General Nambiar has repeatedly stressed to the authorities in Belgrade and Knin that it is UNPROFOR that exercises the protection function in the United Nations Protected Areas and that the presence of these paramilitary units is contrary to the United Nations peace plan and has caused the Croatian army to retain some of its forces at the confrontation line. As a result, clashes continue to occur along the line, fueling intercommunal tension in the United Nations Protected Areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please be shown paragraph 3 under (a), the main incidents in the period covered by the report. That's the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you read for us what the main incident under (a) is in this particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On 7 August 1992, fighting erupted in an area adjacent to the south-eastern portion of Sector West, apparently due to attempts by armed elements of the Croatian side to cross the Sava River and attack Bosnian Serb elements south of the river. United Nations troops in the area were caught in an exchange of fire that included use of tanks, artillery, and mortars; fortunately, there were no United Nations casualties. A significant feature of this incident was that nine bodies in a variety of uniforms found on the southern side of the Sava River were not claimed by either side, which gives -- which gave rise to suspicion that they may have been those of mercenaries."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the text under (d), the next incident.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the last week of August 1992, a large group of armed personnel, who were attempting to infiltrate through Sector North to the Bihac-Cazin area in Bosnia and Herzegovina, were engaged by the local Serb militia and a number were killed or captured. Prisoners interviewed by UNPROFOR said that they had been mobilised and trained by the Croatian army in certain areas of Croatia and were being infiltrated in small groups into Bosnia and Herzegovina to join in the fighting there. This matter was raised with President Tudjman of Croatia on 31st of August, 1992, by Under-Secretary-General Marrack Goulding. The President said that such practices would no longer be permitted. Tension in the area, however, remains high and the incident has been used by the Serbs in the United Nations Protected Areas to substantiate their fears of attacks launched against them from Croatian-held territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you know that UNPROFOR and UN sitpol [as interpreted] reports that this was an armed group of 600 men, the one you just mentioned, the one that was infiltrated from Croatia into Sector North which was not stopped by UNPROFOR -- or rather, my question to you is: Do you know that this was a large group of men?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the details, but if the Secretary-General of the United Nations reported to the Security Council, it must have been an important incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the operation Miljevacki Plateau, Mr. Theunens, on the 21st of June, 1992, and the action by the Croatian army where 40 TO members were killed and were -- their bodies were disposed into pits?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I mention in my examination, I am familiar with the Croatian incursion or operation, the Miljevac Plateau area which was located in the pink zone of Sector South. I've seen a document, I think it's a copy of a letter Milan Martic sent to Boutros Boutros-Ghali in which Milan Martic complained about the 40 TO members who were being killed and treated as Mr. Milovancevic has just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in this same report you just quoted in paragraph 8, and if you believe we have to read it out here we can do so. But to keep short and save time, I can say that Undersecretary-General of the UN, Marrack Goulding, had agreed for the demobilisation of units in Knin to take place, and that the demobilisation be done in two stages, the first was supposed to end by the 20th of September and the second by the 15th of October. However, when the report was drafted on the 28th of September, 1992, the first stage had not been completed as yet.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, that's what paragraph 8 mentions. Now, if we want to see to what extent and later on the demilitarisation or demobilisation of the PJM was implemented or not, we would have to consult the subsequent reports of the Secretary-General to the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 128 of your report, under (b), this is in section 4, did you not say that: "In October and November 1992, an order was issued to enter amendments to the to the organisation of the TO units -- or rather, special police units and to transform the units into the SVK or rather the Serbian army of Krajina"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, and the order I referred to in this summary is 65 ter number 1367 which is discussed on page 146 of the English version of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 143 under 3 do you not say that General Mile Novakovic, commander of the SVK, issued an order on the 27th of November, 1992, for the re-organising of the Territorial Defence and the special police into the Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours -- indeed, Your Honours, I mentioned it, but it's page 146, not 143.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I meant page 146. Thank you. On page 147, paragraph (d), in the line which reads -- paragraph 6, does it say: "The Serbian army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina shall keep and maintain its weapons and equipment in depots with the presence of UNPROFOR representatives according to the Vance plan"? And does paragraph (c) at the top state in the last part of the sentence that: "All the previous establishments of the staffs and units of the Territorial Defence and the special police units of the Republic of Serbian Krajina are hereby disbanded"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. They are disbanded because a new structure has been established, and this new structure is the SVK, the Serbian army of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: So the agreement with Mr. Goulding stipulated the 15th of October, whereas this was done in November. The police units were disbanded in late November. Is that correct, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think that the agreement that Mr. Goulding aimed at, transforming one structure -- one armed structure into another armed structure because at that time the Vance plan was still being applied or should have been applied. And according to the Vance plan, the local Serbs were only allowed to keep a lightly armed police. TO or other armed forces had to be demobilised, demilitarised, and disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with the Vance plan, did the UN have an obligation to protect the area under the UN protection, including the Serb population, and they failed to do that, both at the Miljevac Plateau and when a group of 600 people went through Sector North in August?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only -- I can only mention what the Vance plan says. It says that the people in the UNPAs should be protected from the fear of armed attack. Now, as I stipulated already, Miljevac was not located in the UNPA but was located in the pink zone, and there's a significant difference between the UNPA and the pink zone. Pink zones were areas which were under the control of the JNA and which had in a number of cases, significant Serb presences, but they were located outside the border -- the agreed border of the UNPA. So UNPROFOR had no mandate in the pink zones. It is only as a result of negotiations with the Croatian side and the Serbian side that UNPROFOR started to patrol the pink zones in order to show the flag and to show some reassurances. But, as I mentioned, the pink zones were not part of the UNPAs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If we accept that it is indeed so, even if it was so, does this authorise the Croatian side to kill 40 people and to throw them into a pit in the presence of international forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know whether they were, as it is put here, "thrown in a pit in the presence of international forces." And to answer the question: Obviously not. And I think when you look at the report of the Secretary-General of the United Nations to the Security Council, earlier reports than this one, the Secretary-General clearly alerts the Security Council about the negative effects the Croatian military operation in Miljevac has on the overall situation and the risks it may entail for the future situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We shall now turn, Mr. Theunens, to page 168, which speaks about the relations between the Army of Republika Srpska and Army of Serbian Krajina. When you discuss political aspects, under item 1 you mention a declaration dated the 31st of October, 1992, Prijedor declaration; and under item 2 you speak of a joint defence council, which was established on the 20th of February, 1995, which was supposed to be in charge of the defence of people and the territory in the two Serbian territories west of Drina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, but I don't know what is meant with "the two Serbian territories west of Drina."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I can't explain that to you, Mr. Theunens, even though I know that this refers to Republika Srpska and Serbian Krajina. Let us now turn to page 169. When speaking of military aspects, you mention Operation Corridor 92 under item 1. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you explained that Posavina, that is to say the corridor, is of a vital importance for the survival of the western part of the RS and the RSK and that this is the only land linking Krajina, Western Slavonia, and the Western part of BH with Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who severed the corridor and how? Does it done by Croatian forces which came to the territory of another country and used their forces to cut the corridor in half?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I explained my understanding of the operations in the Posavina corridor during examination, where I mentioned that in the course of April 1992 Bosnian Serbs start taking over the municipalities in -- located in the eastern part of the corridor. We are talking about municipalities like Bijeljina, Zvornik, parts of Brcko, Bosanski Samac. Bosnian Serbs take these over with the assistance of -- elements of -- or armed elements of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, as well as volunteers/paramilitaries from -- who came from Serbia and who had also recruited local forces. And based on what Radovan Karadzic said in May at the 16th Assembly Session of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the establishment of a corridor between Krajina and Semberija was one of the six strategic goals of the Bosnian Serbs. Now, whether anyone severed the corridor, my understanding is that the corridor was established in June 1992, and what I mean by that 234 -- at end of June/July 1992, Bosnian Serbs and forces from the entity known as RSK undertook military operations to free a corridor and to establish their control over that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can it be said that you give extensive answers to the questions concerning which you already provided answers when examined by the Prosecution. You are thus stripping us of valuable times -- of valuable time. Will you now please answer my question? I asked you whether the Croatian forces cut the corridor, and what I expected from you is a simple yes or no answer. I don't need the entire history of that event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Milovancevic, you are also repeating what he has already said in his report and you are making in court things that are already in evidence. How different are you from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I'm asking the witness right now, namely, whether the forces of the Republic of Croatia came out beyond the borders of their own country and crossed into the neighbouring country, Bosnia-Herzegovina, conducted a combat operation there, and cut the corridor in half, is something that this witness has never mentioned, either in his testimony or in his written report. I asked him this because we have an exhibit on 65 ter list, number 711, indicating that the forces of 103rd and 108th Brigade, Zagreb Brigade, and Rijeka Brigade of the Croatian army were deployed in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina in order to conduct an operation there. In addition to that there was 132nd Osijek Brigade there and 109th Djakovica Brigade as well. I'm now asking the witness whether he came across such information before or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it is something that he hasn't mentioned before, then he is not repeating himself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I may have come across this information, but as I mentioned at the outset of my testimony, this report focuses on the SAO Krajina and the RSK Territorial Defence and, subsequently, the SVK. And the relation between these organisations, armed organisations, and Milan Martic. I did not analyse the involvement or the role or activities of Croatian or Bosnian Croat armed forces in general, and certainly not specifically in relation to the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question. Do you have any information indicating that the corridor had been severed and that this is why they attempted a breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think that Mr. Milovancevic and myself seem to understand each other. If you are asking me when the corridor was severed, I know from my previous work that -- I think in November 1992 and December 1992, there was a lot of pressure from Bosnian Croat and also Croatian forces, so HV, from the Osijek pocket, which is located north of the corridor, to cut the corridor. But I don't think that is the information you are looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the severing of the corridor meant that the Republic of Serbian Krajina was, in reality, strangled in the financial, military, and any other sense because there was no way any supplies, including medical supplies and food supplies, could be delivered there from Yugoslavia. In addition to that, there was also a provision, a no-fly zone established.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in -- it is correct that in the course of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I think it's during the latter half of 1992, a no-fly zone was established over Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is -- and it is also correct that the crossroad was essential for the entity known as the RSK to receive support from Serbia and from the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please be shown exhibit 711 from the 65 ter list of the Prosecution. I'm interested in the following pages: 03015812 and then 03015819.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you have before you a transcript of a television programme of Radio Television Belgrade in which a reporter on page 1, line 25, on the first page that I mentioned, 03015812, says that the breakthrough was commenced on the 12th of June and that the defenders were met by aggressors from the 103rd and 108th Brigade as well as by hundreds of Alija's Mujahedin. Is it correct? Is this what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if you could scroll down a little bit. I'm not sure whether we're on the correct page, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The very beginning of the text, the very beginning of it. I don't know what page it is in English, but it is literally the first page of the document. The last four digits are 5812. This is a transcript of a videotape.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this page it says that Milan Martic has just arrived at the 1st Krajina Corps command. The Krajina Corps's VRS unit with headquarters in Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: It should be 3505 in English, 3505 in English, at the bottom of the page. Would you please read out the words of the reporter. Does he mention the 103rd and 108th Croatian Brigades and hundreds of Alija's Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mentions it, but do you want me to read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes -- no, no. Actually, I'm asking you: Is this mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The reporter from RTV Belgrade states that according to his information "the liberators were met by aggressors from the 103rd and 108th Croatian Brigades and hundreds of Alija's Mujahedins." Now, as I tried to explain earlier and also when I explained how this report has been compiled, I tried to find as many original sources as possible, i.e., in talking about the operations, if I had been to -- if I were to analyse the Croatian operations or the alleged Croatian operations in the corridor, I would have looked for military documents and I would not have limited myself to the opinion of one TV reporter because a -- a group known as Alija's Mujahedins, I know more or less what the reporter is talking about, but to me, if I have to assess the reliability of the source, he wouldn't score very high because it's like calling all Serbs "Chetniks" or calling all Croats "Ustashas." He doesn't assist to try to identify and try to determine what happened in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 831 of this report, the reporter talks to a captured Croatian soldier who says that 101st, 108th, and 101st, 109th, and 132nd Brigade were all on the ground. Does this information mean anything to you, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I had known under which conditions this Croatian soldier allegedly made this statement, that would have been very helpful because, again, is this the result of an interrogation? Is it a media interview? Is the person under pressure? All we can say is that we need more sources in order to establish what really happened. I don't doubt that there were military operations in the corridor at that time, and military operations involves various sides. But I cannot, as an analyst, draw any conclusions just based on a media report where words like, or expressions like "Alija's Mujahedins" are being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this same report mentions the statement given by the captured Croatian soldier and says that there were between 4 and 500 mercenaries on the Croatian side, mostly from Germany and also a lot from Turkey, and that it is these Mujahedin that are referred to. It is not used in a derogatory sense, as you are trying to imply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, what does "Mujahedin" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in Arabic this means a fighter for faith, literally. That's what it means, for Islamic faith, for Allah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May -- thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. The question was directed to the witness. You are not in the box, you see. You are not in the witness stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I misunderstood what you wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, I can agree with the definition proposed by Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are fighters of the faith?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, that's how it should be used. But, again, looking at this report, I don't know what Alija's Mujahedins are. It is mentioned there, but do they mean -- and hundreds of them - a particular faction? For this report, I didn't analyse the presence of volunteers of Muslim faith in Bosnia-Herzegovina who participate in the conflict for religious reasons. There is no doubt that there were there. There is even an indictment in this Tribunal against such people or people in control of them. But in this report, I cannot say. I have no information of whether they were really there; it is just a media report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that due to the fact that all communication was severed between Serbia and Serbian Krajina, 12 babies in incubators in Banja Luka died because they did not have oxygen supplies, that kidney patients died because they did not have supplies for dialysis, that the Republic of Serbian Krajina sent urgent appeals to the international community to open up the corridor; however, they received no response. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've seen media reports from the RSK media about this, but again, there's not much I can say about it. If it happened, it's very sad, but that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Martic was promoted to the rank of colonel general after this operation. Do you know that Mr. Martic refused to accept that rank and that he in fact never became colonel-general because he believed that it was his duty to serve his people, not to attempt to obtain higher ranks for himself?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that may well be true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, the question is: Do you know or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've seen reports, media reports, where indeed Martic said: I'm not interested in that rank. But I haven't seen any revocation of the order that is included in my report that appointed him to that rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Have you seen any official decline of the offer by Mr. Martic in the records that you read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I haven't seen any such decline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see a document promoting Mr. Martic to the rank of colonel-general? There is an order by the president of the republic, which is normally followed by a promotion, which is a special ceremony promoting him to a general. Have you seen any documents regarding that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've only seen the order by Goran Hadzic, who was then president of the RSK, appointing or nominating Milan Martic to the rank of colonel-general. Now, when it comes to other officers, there was always only one single document I've seen, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 173, Mr. Theunens, you speak of the Pauk command or spider command, and you say that on the 23rd of September, the Assembly of Velika Kladusa established a commission on establishing an autonomous province of Western Bosnia headed by Fikret Avdic, following which hostilities broke out between the pro-Sarajevo 5th Corps and the forces of Western Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what does this term "pro-Sarajevo" mean, the one referring to the 5th Corps? Is this the 5th Corps of Bosnia and Herzegovina, whose president is Alija Izetbegovic? Or does this refer to something else? What does "pro-Sarajevo" mean?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean by this the 5th Corps of the ABiH which were the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but at that time Bosnia-Herzegovina was -- there was a war happening and there were basically three factions fighting each other. There were Bosnian Serbs, who had the VRS; there were the Bosnian Croats, who had the HVO; and then there were -- I wouldn't say "the others," but mainly people who were known as Muslims, i.e., the nationality Muslim, as well as non-Muslims -- I mean, sometimes these Muslims call themselves "Bosniaks," so you could call them "Bosniak" or "non-Bosniaks" who believed in the unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina and wanted to keep Bosnia and Herzegovina together as one state, and their armed force was called the ABiH. So I agree that the term I used in my report was a bit of an oversimplification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did the army of BH intervene militarily in order to prevent [Realtime transcript read in error "implement"] the implementation of the decision on declaring the autonomous province of Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you meant in order to prevent the implementation of the decision on declaring the western province of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I didn't study this in great detail for my report, but I remember from the documents I looked at, both at the ICTY and before, that quite soon after Abdic declared his autonomous province of Western Bosnia, an armed conflict erupted in the area known as the Bihac pocket between forces under the control of Abdic and the 5th Corps which was commanded by Atif Dudakovic, which was loyal to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 178 did you explain under paragraph (e) that pursuant to the operations log for Pauk command, it stems that it was established in November of 1994 in order to restore the autonomous province of Western Bosnia after it collapsed on the 20th of August, 1994?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that -- or rather, when the autonomous province of Western Bosnia collapsed on the 20th of August, 1994, that 70.000 Muslims who had lived in the area fled from the ABiH army into the RSK so that the RSK had to open up all its food supplies to feed 70.000 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is outside the framework of my report, but I remember from my work as an intelligence analyst in Belgium at the time, that indeed the significant number of people loyal to Abdic had to flee. They wanted to flee -- they wanted actually to enter Croatia, but they were stopped by the Croats at the limits of Sector North, and I think there were two, not really camps, but two areas where they stayed. One was the Turanj crossing and other, I think, was a chicken farm called Batnoga. And I think it's correct that the RSK provided assistance in the first instance, but after a while the UN had to provide assistance. When I was working for UNPROFOR I went to the area myself, I mean to Batnoga, and people were living in appalling conditions, but then all the assistance was being provided by the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the Croatian side refused to receive the Muslims fleeing their death or pogrom that was a threat coming from the 5th Corps, but the Croatian side refused and they were finally received in the RSK. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not hundred per cent certain of the circumstances under which these people fled and whether it would be justified to use the words Mr. Milovancevic has used, but the situation was that they -- these people remained stuck at the Turanj crossing and Batnoga. Turanj is just south of Karlovac, if you look at the map, and indeed they were taken care of there by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 139 under paragraph (f) you state that the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Republika Srpska closely cooperated on the political and military level.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, but that's the summary what follows in the report and it's more specifically dealt with on pages 168 and the following pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As a member of UNPROFOR, did you write a report on the 7th of March, 1995, which is listed as exhibit 1467 on the OTP list where you precisely deal with the matters of the creation of the joint defence council? Can this exhibit 1467 please be shown on the screen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall writing under item 7 -- or, I apologise, item 6 of the report that the developments -- the political developments so far are a consequence, and I paraphrase, of the Tudjman declaration on the future of UNPROFOR in Croatia which have prompted the leadership of the RSK and the Serbian Republic of BiH to reinforce their links?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In item 7, do you state that: "In the past during the Croatian offensive in Maslenica or the operation against the Medak pocket, 9th September 1993, there has been no tangible support of the Bosnian Serbian army for the army of Serbian Krajina, and that the main reason for that was the fact that none of the sides had the means available to assist the other because the Bosnian forces did not have enough manpower, whereas the forces of the RSK, as you put it in item 8, needed all their troops and weaponry on the home front?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, and this -- I mean, the entire memorandum is based on the information we had available at the UNPROFOR headquarters at that moment in time. It may well be that now, because I have access to additional information, I may change certain parts of that report or add certain information to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you state in paragraph 11 that the declaration dated 20th February in Banja Luka was to lead to significant changes in the current situation and that its objectives were primarily political, because both the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Republika Srpska wanted to show their solidarity toward the outside world, Croatia, and Serbia in particular?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- to quote the paragraph 11 correctly, it should be stated that for the time being there are no indications that the 20th February Banja Luka declaration will lead to a major change in the current situation. I forgot the exact date of that -- of when I drafted that memorandum, but again, that was a first assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the annex to this report dated 4th March, 1995, under item 2, did you not write that the Republic of Serbian Krajina largely depends on the economical support from Serbia and Republika Srpska and - this is the last line of item 2 - that they depend on the supplies coming from the outside of Republika Srpska, that's to say in terms of fuel?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me, Your Honours, but it is correct. And maybe I should add that the RSK also largely depended the support provided by UNPROFOR, and I mean by that mainly humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What was the basis for you saying in the initial part of section 4 that cooperation between the RSK and the RS was quite extensive, politically and militarily, if in your report in 1995 you state that their cooperation was quite poor, that they were only able to give a show of political support but otherwise were unable to secure sufficient resources for themselves?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is not really a correct reflection of my report, my -- the expert report here, and the memorandum I drafted in 1995. As I mentioned earlier, in 1995 and, for example, the issue of Pauk is a very good example. Within UNPROFOR we were never able to establish whether there was organised support from the RSK, organised military support with combat units, weapons, and other military supplies from the RSK, so the SVK, to Abdic's forces. It's only after -- once I came here that I discovered original military documents indicating that indeed there was an organised support of the RSK to the Abdic forces in cooperation with the Bosnian Serbs and the Republic of Serbia. At the time, I mean in 1995, in the UNPROFOR headquarters we believed that this support was mainly a local initiative because of the black-market connections. We new very well that the Lika corps was conducting black-market with the BiH. We also know that other SVK units in the area, the Banja Corps and the Kordun Corps were involved in black-market activities with Abdic's forces. We also knew that there were helicopter flights from Zagreb to the Bihac pocket in order to bring in supplies for Dudakovic's forces for the 5th Corps. We were always surprised by the SVK did no efforts to shoot down these helicopters. Now, coming -- I apologise for this long answer, but I think it maybe helps to explain the circumstances under which this memorandum was drafted when I was in Zagreb. When two entities decide to create a joint defence council and make a number of statements in -- to say: Well, we have now a common defence, I think that this is an example of significant political cooperation, and this is actually what I mentioned in my report. The fact -- the fact that on the ground at that time when I was in Zagreb, we had no reliable or credible information about organised units being involved in carrying out mutual support, well, okay, that's how it was then. Now with the additional information I've seen while working at the ICTY, I may have to review what is mentioned in this 1995 memorandum, and I think that is quite understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the exhibit 1467 please be admitted as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence as an exhibit. Can it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 110, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the strength of the Croatian forces attacking Western Slavonia on the 1st of May, 1995, was?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only give a quite general answer because I didn't analyse it in detail because it's not part of the subject matter of my report, but I think that the forces of two guards brigades as well as one regular HV brigade and also special police forces were involved on the Croatian side. But I can't give a more precise figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you review OTP document 1472, as listed on the 65 ter exhibit list, which is the report of the Main Staff of the RSK army dated 4th May 1995, which stated that the 18th Corps which was in Western Slavonia had 4.700 men --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can he just answer that question hat you put first before you put another question? We've got a very short lunch break. I would like us to break punctually. Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, but I don't know which is 65 ter number 1472, so it would be helpful if I could see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible, then, Mr. Milovancevic, that you help the witness to see the document when we come back from lunch?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We shall adjourn and come back at half past 2.00. Court adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One thing briefly in terms of schedule. I know that we're trying to finish with Mr. Theunens today, and I just wanted to forecast for the Defence and the Court that I think I have about 15 minutes or so of re-direct examination, including dealing with the time-line that Your Honours had asked about earlier and a few other matters. I just wanted to alert the Defence, so hopefully it can be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hopefully you can do that, Mr. Milovancevic. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will take the schedule into consideration. I will keep it in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you told us that you learned some information about the strength of the Croatian forces attacking Sector West, the zone under the protection of the UN on the 1st of May, 1995. Do you know what the balance of forces was of the two sides, the Croatian side attacking and the other side defending?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do not know what the exact balance of forces was. I think also it would be -- it may well be misleading to only base ourselves on figures like troop strength and so on, because from the documents I reviewed for this report, in particular the investigation commissions that were established -- or the reports by the investigation commissions that were established in the RSK, following the fall of Western Slavonia, it appears the 18th Corps was not as well-organised and as well motivated as it could have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you know that General Bobetko, chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian army published his book where he stated that the directive for the implementation of Flash operation number 5/94 was issued on the 15th of December, 1994, and that three months before the operation was implemented the Croatian forces positioned themselves on the points from where they were supposed to launch the attack, in his words?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't analyse or use the book of Bobetko for this report. Had as you can see from the report it doesn't include an analysis about the activity of the Croatian forces either. Now, from my recollection from my work from the UNPROFOR in Zagreb, we found that out of operations the corps had conducted for several weeks, but I would not in a position to confirm or offer a comment on the allegations made in the book of Bobetko or the information provided in the book of Bobetko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you learned which were the main axes of attack of the Croatian force in Operation Flash, which started on the 1st of May, 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I refer to the previous reply. I didn't analyse the Operation Flash for the purpose of this report. What I remember from information I saw at the time when I worked in UNPROFOR was that Croatian forces approached from along the highway, both from the east as well as from the west. And I also believe that there were some forces approaching from the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If you did not analyse the information or look for the information, then what is the basis for your conclusion as to what the conduct of the Serbian side was, whether they defended themselves well or not? If you do not have any information as to what the conduct and the acts of the Serbian side were, what's the basis of the conclusions you state in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to draw your attention on the 65 ter numbers 1889 and 1890, which are mentioned or discussed on the pages 199 to pages 202 of my report. These are quite extensive documents. I think they cover each 20 pages, something. One is a report by a civilian investigation commission, officially called the Republic of Serbian Krajina State Fact-finding Commission on the Causes and the Manner of the Fall of Western Slavonia. The other one is a military investigation commission, and it is exactly in these two reports that I found information on the conduct, morale, and the -- the way how the 18 Corps -- but also other senior officials in the SVK General Staff, as well as Milan Martic, how they conducted the operations. So it is not something I invent, it is something that comes from these two investigation reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you invented them, Mr. Theunens, but, rather, that you did not assess the balance of the two warring parties. Can you tell me, did the UNPROFOR command assess the Croatian Operation Flash? Can you tell us anything about it? Since the zone under the protection of the UN was attacked and since UNPROFOR moved out of the way of the Croatian forces and allowed them to launch an attack and seize the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this description of the alleged reaction or action of UNPROFOR does not correspond with my recollection. It is indeed correct that after the operation within the headquarters studies were made and also reports were drafted on the -- on the way how the UNPROFOR battalions in Sector West acted prior, during, and after the Croatian attack. Now, I'm not familiar with the conclusions of these reports. What I can also maybe mention, it -- excuse me? -- is that prior to the operations, UNPROFOR was both within the sector as well as outside, and that outside applies to the military observers, subject to serious restrictions in its freedom of movement. And, for example, what I -- when I mentioned earlier that we found out that the Croats had been preparing weeks ahead, it is only too late that we understood -- I mean we, that UNPROFOR headquarters understood that the visits by what seemed to be civilians during the weekend to certain locations close to the zone of separation and to the contact line in Sector West, that these were not refugees, Croatian refugees, who came to look for their houses, but actually military personnel and special police personnel in civilian clothes who came to prepare and carry out reconnaissance operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Were such refugees offered by Croatian President Tudjman to the RSK when he insisted that only such type of Croat refugees return to the area whilst refusing to allow Serb refugees to return to the area? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, analysing statements, Croatian President -- late-Croatian President Tudjman may have made in relation to Croatian refugees was not part of the tasking I received when I drafted this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Defence exhibit 1D000111 be shown on the screen. This is a report by UNPROFOR, an overview of activities of the Croatian offensive against Sector West on the 1st of May. The report details incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: While this is being done, to save time, let's proceed. The report says that the Croatian army launched attacks from three directions: North, east, and west, that the main axis of attack from the east was along Gorice-Pivare highway, that the attack was supported by armoured vehicles, artillery, mortars. That the main axis of attack from the west was Novska highway-Donji Rajici, that the attack was supported by armoured vehicles and artillery, that the main axis of attack from the north was Pakrac, Glavinice [phoen], Seovica, Brusnik, and that the area of Pakrac was subject to heavy shelling that very morning and on several occasions during the day along the Dragovici road. Do we have the exhibit on the screen? Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's another document, Your Honours, because this document talks about 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: 1D000111. Do you know about this data, Mr. Theunens, that late at night the Croatian side informed on the eve of the attack the UNPROFOR command structure in Sector West, that combat operations would ensue, advising them to place UNPROFOR units under their command in a safe location. Are you familiar with such a document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have seen the document at the time, but I didn't review it to compile the expert report I'm testifying on here. I remember from the events at the time that we were warned, I think, at 4.00 in the morning or 5.00 in the morning -- we received the phone call to join the headquarters in Zagreb. I mean from time point of view, that's the only thing I recall. And indeed the troops in the area had been warned in advance. Now whether this warning came from the HV to the UNPROFOR headquarters in Zagreb or from the HV directly to the troops in Sector West, that is something I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence as Defence exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the -- excuse me. May the document be admitted into evidence as Defence exhibit, and may it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 111, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see on the screen Defence exhibit 1D000118.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Before the document comes up, Mr. Theunens, I would like to put to you that this document has to do with "an incident," as it was termed in the document. The document is dated the 4th of May, 1995 - an incident which occurred during the humanitarian efforts to avoid any casualties among civilian population. This has to do with an event in the village of Gavrenica in the Pakrac area. Do we have it on the screen now? Yes, we do. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black is on his feet, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just -- again, as has happened before, this is a document I have never seen before as far as I know. We weren't notified that it was going to be used. And if Mr. Milovancevic intends to use this and make it an exhibit, I would appreciate it if he would explore who made this. Because what you have is what seems to be one document and then if you can scroll a little bit to the top of the page, this and the last document have titles added which don't seem to be part of the same -- the body of the document. And if we could have an explanation as to where these come from, it would help me know as to whether I need to object to them. Again, I need to see these before they're put to the witness, otherwise I'm going to have to ask for an adjournment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are the documents -- photocopies of UNPROFOR documents which can be found in the book called "Serbian Western Slavonia, May 1995: Expulsion." This was published by Veritas, which is an non-governmental organisation dealing with the events in Western Slavonia. Pursuant to the author of this book, all documents and statements contained in it were sent to the Prosecution back in 1997. In this case, on the monitor we can see a document, a photocopy actually of a document of the UN. I think that it is beyond dispute that this is a UN document. It bears all proper marks. It has a typical introduction, signature --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute, Mr. Milovancevic. You say this book -- this document comes from -- was sent to the Prosecution back in 1997. Sent to the Prosecution by whom? And has notice been given that they are going to be used as evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what we see now is part of a document coming from this book. I mentioned the name of the book. The author of this book states that he sent all of these documents, all of these statements, to the OTP, all of the documents contained in this book, and I am now putting to the witness one of such documents. Namely, he claims that this was sent to the Prosecution. Naturally, this is a separate issue from the one raised by my learned friend from the Prosecution, namely that we need to inform them about the documents we intend to use. This issue has not been resolved yet. Yes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a problem, Mr. Milovancevic. Obviously this -- you say this book was sent to the Prosecution. I'm not quite sure what you mean by the Prosecution. Was it sent to this Prosecutor for the purposes of this case or was it sent to the offices of the OTP for their general information? I don't -- if this document is not part of the documents that have been disclosed, surely it must be tendered into evidence in terms of proper procedure. In other words, the author of the book must come here and tender it. You can't testify from the -- from the bar and tell us that the author of the book sent this document to a -- to the OTP. The author must come here and say: This is my document. I am the author of this. I certify that -- I stand by the contents of this document and I sent it to the OTP for the following purposes. And only that way can it be admitted into evidence. I'm not quite sure what you mean by "the author sent it to the OTP." I would like you to explain that even before we deal with the actual issue raised by Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just attempted to give you an explanation contained in this book and inform you and our learned friends from the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Obviously the explanation you gave doesn't answer the question I raised; that's why I'm repeating myself in different words. I'm saying to you: When you say "this book was sent to the OTP by the author," you are testifying. And you are not in the witness box. You cannot be cross-examined on that statement to find out the veracity of the statement. My -- to my knowledge, exhibits -- the proper way for exhibits -- for tendering exhibits is that the author or the receiver of the document must come here and say: I wrote this document. I confirm the contents of this document, and I'm available to be cross-examined on the contents of this document. That way it can be admitted. Or: I am the recipient of this document, it came from so-and-so, who then addressed it to me, and this is the original. When you say -- you have explained -- your explanation, in my understanding, is not procedural. You see, this document is different, Mr. Milovancevic, if I may just add, from the other documents that you have said came from the OTP and were given to the Defence in this case. This is a document that is coming completely, it looks like, from the Defence side. And the Defence must tender the document properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just clarify. The most important thing from our point of view is notice. I may not object to the authenticity of this document, and I think, in fairness to the Defence, the rules of this Tribunal are much more lax than they are in -- certainly in my home jurisdiction about admission of documents without strict proof of authenticity. But what concerns me is a document such as this one and the last one is that they obviously have information added. We're not dealing with an original document. The title from the last document was something like "The UN on the Run." That clearly seems to me is not part of the UN document that -- that is reproduced there perhaps faithfully by the authors. So that's why it's difficult for us as the Prosecution without advanced notice that these documents are going to be used to be able to determine what's acceptable and what's not acceptable. For instance, if Mr. Milovancevic could say for us that those titles are not part of the document but the rest is -- is a true photocopy, I may very well be willing to accept that and not object to the admission. But it's the kind of thing that's very difficult to do on the fly. And I know that there's a motion about this, but this is my concern about this with this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Black I think has explained his concern about the document and he does tell me that admission of documents is slightly different in the Tribunal. He has raised this issue earlier about advanced notice. Obviously he's now taken by surprise if documents are being produced about which he has no advance notice, of which he hasn't seen before, and the intention is to have them admitted into evidence. He had made this request a couple of days ago, Mr. Milovancevic. You undertook to try and do that as best you could; it doesn't seem to have been done this time. Now, from what I understand from what he's saying, he's not able to react to this document because he doesn't know it. So he needs to know it first before it is put here. This might cause an adjournment right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point in time, I'm trying to offer into evidence documents contained in this book which has a title, just like a book by General Kadijevic had a title. It was entitled "My View of a Break-up," and it also contained some documents. Likewise, this book entitled "Western Slavonia, May 1995: Exodus," contains a number of documents. The author of the book gave titles to some of the documents. The titles are not part of original documents, and I will point this out to the witness. What I attempted to tell the Trial Chamber is that the Defence has not disclosed this document to the Prosecution, not yet. However, in the very book, the author - and I'm not trying to testify about this - the author claims that he sent this book to the Prosecution. That is not identical to disclosure. I realise that. And I'm not trying to claim that it is. But I don't see why we shouldn't take a look at this document which is contained in this book in the form of a photocopy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The reason we are not able to take this book at this point is because the Prosecution says they have no advance notice of it, they do not know how they should react to the suggested tender of the document into evidence, whether to object or to accept it, and they can only be able to do so once they have seen the book, which is the reason why they've been asking for advanced notices. Does that make it clearer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear to me, Your Honours. However, I understood the words of my learned friend from the Prosecution in a somewhat different light, and let me clarify this. Could my learned friend state his position, namely, do they object to documents from this book being put to the witness or not? I will abide by your ruling, but I don't think that my learned friend stated firmly his opposition. And would he please clarify his position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think your learned friend stated his position quite clearly. His position is clearly that he is unable to react because he doesn't know the document. He hasn't seen the document, and I think the solution to this problem is either to take a stand-down of about five, ten minutes so that we can show your learned friend that document and he can make up his mind whether he wants to object or not object.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I can help. At this point, based on what Mr. Milovancevic has said, that the titles are not part of the documents, I don't want to hold things up further. I'm happy to continue. I do not object to this document with the understanding with that that title is not part of the document, and then I hope we can discuss it -- well, we'll try to reach agreement between the parties. There's also a pending motion on this issue, and then going forward from -- to that, I think we can resolve it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would then -- the Chamber would rule then that it comes in as an MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
